name: Aeronca C-2 / C-3 / K Scout
summary: Early Aeronca light planes: the C-2 and C-3 were tiny wire-braced 'flying bathtubs', and the K Scout of 1937 brought a conventional enclosed cabin.

wings: High wing braced by wires from a pylon over the cabin on C-2/C-3; strut-braced on the K
engines: Tiny two-cylinder (or small four-cylinder) engine up front
Cylinder heads often poke out of the short cowl
fuselage: C-3 has a raised 'razorback' spine and a bathtub-like side-by-side cockpit; the Master has a rounded back and enclosed cabin
Fixed tailwheel gear with external struts on the early models

tellTales: Tiny prewar high-wing with bracing wires instead of lift struts (C-2/C-3)
Small engine with cylinders poking out of a short nose
Raised razorback spine behind a bathtub-like cockpit

confusedWith.howToTell: The Champ is a postwar tandem two-seater with lift struts and a fully cowled flat-four; the C-3 has bracing wires, a bathtub cockpit and a tiny engine.
The Chief is a rounder postwar side-by-side two-seater with lift struts and a proper cowled engine; the C-3 is smaller and wire-braced.
The J-3 has V-struts and a fully cowled flat-four with tandem seats; the C-3 has wires, side-by-side seats and a tiny engine.
The J-2/E-2 is a tandem V-strut Cub design; the C-2/C-3 has wire bracing and side-by-side or bathtub seating.
